species.name: Aluminum monohydride
species.exclusion: This review does not concern AlH3, AlH ions, or condensed aluminum hydride.

scope: Scientific provenance and candidate assessment. No runtime or curated-data adoption is made in this investigation.

sources.inspection: Full AlH page (printed p 114, PDF page 56) rendered and visually read, including constants, comments, references, and six tabulated rows.
sources.ancestry: The note adopts Gaydon (1953), D0=2.9±0.2 eV, from vibrational extrapolation and A-state predissociation. It mentions a 3.05 eV linear Birge-Sponer extrapolation and a 3.07 eV predissociation limit. Thermal functions use Zeeman and Ritter (1954) molecular constants, X1Sigma+ weight 1 and symmetry 1.
references: A. G. Gaydon, Dissociation Energies, 2nd edition, Chapman and Hall, London (1953).
P. B. Zeeman and G. J. Ritter, Canadian Journal of Physics 32, 555 (1954).
sources.limit: The underlying 1953 book and 1954 article were not independently inspected. The review does not reinterpret the printed ±20 kJ/mol estimate as a calibrated statistical confidence interval. Printed/online agreement is demonstrated only at the six transcribed nodes.

sources.inspection: Printed pp 3 and 10 visually inspected. The AlH table predates the third edition and therefore uses the 1973 CODATA constants.
sources.limit: Modern constants may be used for a separate common-convention comparison, but should not be silently presented as the original JANAF constants.

sources.inspection: Official report Appendix D records and bibliography inspected. ALH printed p 49, AL p 46, H p 126.
sources.ancestry: ALH cites Gurvich, Veyts and Alcock (1996), Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Substances, volume 3, Begell House, part 1 p 139 and part 2 p 106. AL cites Cox 1989/Kaufman 1991b/Gordon 1999; H cites Herzberg 1970/Moore 1972/Gordon 1999.
sources.limit: Gurvich part 1 p 139 and part 2 p 106 were not recovered. The report establishes the NASA record and source citation, not the full primary experimental selection or its uncertainty. The prior major-molecule fixture lists a 300 K lower bound; the official ALH record starts at 200 K.

sources.title: Lifetimes and predissociation in AlH(AlD) A1Pi
sources.citation: P. Baltayan and O. Nedelec, Journal of Chemical Physics 70, 2399–2403 (1979).
sources.inspection: User-provided publisher PDF, six PDF pages including cover. Complete article printed pp 2399-2403 read; printed p 2399 abstract and p 2401 equations/figure/table visually checked.
sources.findings: Both the printed abstract (p 2399) and Section IV (p 2401) report De(X)=3.16+/-0.01 eV and De(A)=0.24+/-0.01 eV. Section IV lowers the X asymptote by 100 cm^-1 relative to A for Al(2P) fine structure; Section V identifies Al(2P)+H(2S) atomic ground terms. The outer potential is inferred from lifetimes/intensity deficits/linewidths with a tunnelling model and spectroscopic RKR/Morse input. The previous registered-abstract value 3.17 eV is a metadata discrepancy resolved in favour of the printed article.
sources.limit: The quoted uncertainty has no defined confidence level. High-J lifetimes and approximately 50 cm^-1 level-energy uncertainty dominate the discussed limitations; Fig. 4 errors exclude the latter. The original uses an approximate 100 cm^-1 atomic splitting without explicit J labels. Do not add a term-center correction already inconsistent with its lower-X-limit convention. Full zero-point and Gurvich reference reconciliation remain separate tasks.

local_pdf.inspection: User-provided publisher PDF, six PDF pages including cover. Complete article printed pp 2399-2403 read; printed p 2399 abstract and p 2401 equations/figure/table visually checked.
local_pdf.archive_policy: The user-provided full article and extracted full text remain local. The repository retains bibliographic metadata, hash, independently written review notes and selected factual quantities only.

sources.inspection: Full author-hosted publisher PDF downloaded; Sections 2.2 and 3, Table 4, and the discussion on printed pp 1408–1410 read.
sources.findings: The X1Sigma+/A1Pi model fits low rovibrational levels. The authors deliberately allow X-state De=3.644 eV to improve the v=0–8 fit; they explicitly reject its physical asymptote accuracy. They quote Baltayan 1979 as 3.16±0.01 eV. Partition functions are explicit state sums at 1 K spacing to 5000 K, with nuclear spin factors 12, 18, 22 for 27AlH, 27AlD, 26AlH.
sources.limit: Use Q/12 for 27AlH in a nuclear-spin-excluded convention. The fitted De is not independent energy evidence. Only X and A are included; higher electronic states and their perturbations are omitted. Agreement with older partition compilations is not proof of complete high-temperature thermochemistry.

sources.citation: Yurchenko et al., MNRAS 527, 9736–9756 (2024), AloHa; inspected arXiv 2312.05958v1 preprint.
sources.inspection: Full preprint downloaded; Sections 4 and 5.1, state definition, and partition-function discussion read.
sources.findings: AloHa improves the X/A rovibronic model and A-state predissociation using laboratory information. Section 5.1 includes bound and quasi-bound states in the partition function and keeps continuum absorption separate. The authors say Q remains close to WYLLoT because the ground state dominates.
sources.limit: The official definition file gives a 5000 K maximum. Neither that limit nor successful low-state spectroscopy proves a complete all-electronic-state partition sum. Higher triplets and other omitted states could affect heat capacity; disagreement with NASA cannot be attributed uniquely to a NASA defect without the Gurvich state inventory.

sources.inspection: Version 20240307 raw definition and matching partition file inspected.
sources.normalization: The nuclear spin product is (2I_Al+1)(2I_H+1)=6×2=12. The X-state electronic multiplicity remains 1; do not multiply by the atomic Al term degeneracy.

sources.citation: Qin, Bai and Liu, Astrophysical Journal 917, 87 (2021).
sources.inspection: Full author-hosted paper read in Sections 2.1 and 3.1 and Tables 1 and 3.
sources.findings: Independent icMRCI+Q calculations yield De=3.190, 3.201, 3.198 eV with AVQZ, AV5Z, AV6Z. Table 1 labels the experimental 3.16±0.01 eV as De and attributes it to Baltayan 1979; this quotation is not another measurement. Experimental omega_e=1682.37 and omega_ex_e=29.05 cm^-1 are attributed to Szajna 2011.
sources.limit: The dissociation limit is labelled Al(2P)+H(2S) without a resolved atomic J. No numerical thermochemical uncertainty is reported. The theory supports the higher-energy direction but does not determine a precise adopted D0.

sources.inspection: Full repository PDF downloaded; Section 3.3 and nuclear-spin convention read.
sources.findings: The atmosphere calculation uses D0=3.16 eV and Q/g_ns. The D0 label conflicts with De in the inspected 1979 printed article and Qin 2021 Table 1.
sources.limit: This is an astrophysical application, not an independent threshold measurement. Its D0 value must not override the De/D0 distinction.

sources.inspection: Full preprint downloaded; Section 2.1.1 and Table 1 column definitions read; AlH numerical row is preserved in the existing major_molecule_reference.json fixture.
sources.findings: The AlH row lists HH 3.060, Luo 2.949±0.130, G2 3.135, and adopted 2.949±0.130 eV. Thus the adopted threshold follows Luo 2007, not a new 2016 dissociation experiment. Molecular Q excludes nuclear spin products.
sources.limit: The specific Luo 2007 AlH original references and uncertainty construction remain uninspected. Do not infer common ancestry with JANAF merely from numerical proximity.

sources.inspection: Official NIST persistent-line level table read on 2026-11-02.
sources.findings: The Al(3s2 3p 2P) J=1/2 and 3/2 levels are at 0 and 112.061 cm^-1, with electronic weights 2 and 4. The term center is therefore about 0.0093 eV above the lowest level.
sources.limit: The modern atomic splitting supports interpretation of the lower X asymptote in the 1979 paper. Its approximately 100 cm^-1 offset is already incorporated; neither a second term-center subtraction nor a precise retrospective correction is justified without reconstructing the potential reference. Gurvich remains uninspected.

sources.inspection: Official web listing identifies 3286 species. Searches of its rendered full text for AlH, HAl, Aluminum, Aluminium gave no matches. Direct file download returned HTTP 403.
sources.finding: No AlH value was located in this inspected version.
sources.limit: This is a version-scoped negative lookup, not proof of absence from every ATcT version.

scientific_assessment.energy: The printed primary De=3.16 eV, less an approximately 0.1034 eV zero-point energy, gives diagnostic D0=3.0566 eV. This is about 0.0064 eV above NASA-derived 3.0502 eV and 0.1148 eV above JANAF-derived 2.9418 eV. The original explicitly incorporates the X/A fine-structure offset; no extra term-center shift is applied. The full text strengthens the preference for a NASA-like energy and resolves the 3.17/3.16 metadata discrepancy, but does not certify the exact NASA value, a statistical uncertainty distribution, or high-temperature thermal functions. Do not adopt 3.16 eV directly as D0.
scientific_assessment.thermal: AloHa Q/12 provides a useful independent spectral-model check through 5000 K, including derivative diagnostics. Agreement or disagreement must be interpreted with its X/A state coverage, quasi-bound treatment, isotope mass, and original physical constants. A few-percent agreement in Q alone does not certify heat capacity.
scientific_assessment.separate_limits: Access uncertainty: Gurvich/Luo pages remain unread; the 1979 full text is now inspected. Reference uncertainty: lower X dissociation limit and inclusion of fine structure are explicit, but exact reconciliation with Gurvich and the original approximate splitting remains open. Spectroscopic uncertainty: +/-0.01 eV has no stated confidence level, and higher zero-point terms remain unpropagated. High-temperature model uncertainty: electronic-state completeness is not certified.
scientific_assessment.next_action: Recover the Gurvich evaluation and Luo entry, align exact atomic/zero-point references and review thermal state contributions before a precise production correction. The 1979 access gap and 3.17/3.16 discrepancy are resolved; stronger evidence for NASA-like binding does not endorse its entire thermal function.
